input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year take-or-pay minimum on us (USD 2,000,000 per year for three years) expressly with no reduction or termination right — the playbook walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 9.4 (our termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with fees only for conforming Services provided) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). We propose deleting the commitment so fees are payable only for Services used or ordered, with the 12-month reducible commitment plus true-up available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Replace the three-year take-or-pay minimum with pay-for-what-is-ordered/used
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment and replaced it with payment for Services used or ordered, consistent with our position against minimum commitments without an exit. It also conflicted with Sections 9.4 (termination for convenience) and 12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment); if a commitment is essential, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term. Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or shortfall obligation.
